世界的インフレについて警鐘を鳴らす

AI技術を運転に適用する
apply ___ intelligence technology to driving

海洋生物の多様性を確保する
ensure a diversity of ___ life

大気中の二酸化炭素を減らす
reduce carbon dioxide in the ___

qs.note: 主語が単数の過去なので started with。 （文中: started with）

qs.q: The budget provided by the company will ___ project to project.
qs.note: vary from A to A =「AごとにAへと異なる」。willの後なので原形。

qs.q: The vaccine ___ another drug and resulted in a deadly side effect.
qs.note: resulted と並ぶ過去形 interacted with。 （文中: interacted with）

qs.q: We need to stop ___ unimportant details or we'll never move the discussion forward.
qs.note: stop +動名詞「〜するのをやめる」→ focusing on。 （文中: focusing on）

qs.q: Some insects succeed in ___ their predators by emitting poisonous chemicals.
qs.note: succeed in +動名詞 → fighting off「撃退する」。 （文中: fighting off）

qs.q: ___ her doctor's advice led to her ruining her health.
qs.note: 文頭の主語＝動名詞、大文字で Tuning out「無視すること」。 （文中: Tuning out）

qs.q: The researchers expected the microbe to ___ moisture.
qs.note: to の後で原形 respond to「〜に反応する」。

qs.q: Some refugees have serious difficulties in ___ a new environment.
qs.note: difficulty in +動名詞 → adapting to「適応する」。 （文中: adapting to）

qs.q: We need to respect the knowledge and experiences that ___ age.
qs.note: 先行詞は複数(knowledge and experiences)、関係詞節で come with「〜と共に生じる」。

qs.q: To get accurate data, we will ___ pre- and post-surveys of the experiment.
qs.note: will の後で原形 carry out「実施する」。

qs.q: One effect of artificial light is that it can be ___ to some marine creatures.
qs.note: 人工光は海洋生物の行動を乱す＝stressful。

qs.q: Tim Smyth and his teammates aimed to identify ___.
opts: the largest chunk of the sea lit up at night
the brightest place in the water
the interactions among life in the ocean
qs.ans: the brightest place in the water
qs.note: "assess where in the water this glow is strongest"＝最も明るい場所。

qs.q: ___ affect the depth to which light can penetrate water.
qs.note: 本文の sediment や tiny floating plants and animals＝小さな海洋生物。

qs.q: The researchers used ___ of copepods to conduct their study.
qs.note: カイアシは光を手がかりにする＝光感受性を利用。

qs.q: Daniel Abram and his colleagues obtained the results by ___.
opts: asking their mothers to speak meaningless words
scanning the brains of young kids
qs.ans: scanning the brains of young kids
qs.note: 7〜16歳の脳をスキャンして得た結果。

qs.q: Mom's voices ___ early teenagers.
qs.note: 思春期初期に母の声の魅力が薄れる(less rewarding)。

qs.q: According to the study on the stressed girls, ___ their stress hormone levels.
opts: a call from their mothers reduced
the voices of their mothers maintained
qs.ans: a call from their mothers reduced
qs.note: 電話で母の声を聞くとストレスホルモンが下がった(text/emailでは効果なし)。

qs.q: According to Abram, teens can't help ignoring their mothers' voice because ___.
opts: their brains are programmed to tune in to unfamiliar voices
they have already been frustrated by miscommunication with them
they have started to depend more on paternal support
qs.ans: their brains are programmed to tune in to unfamiliar voices
qs.note: 脳が見知らぬ声に注意を向けるよう変化するため。

qs.q:
人工の光がどのように海洋生物の正常な行動に影響を与えるのかを知るために、研究者たちはデータを集めた。
Researchers collected data to decide ___ of sea creatures.

「すべての種が光の輝きに等しく敏感だ、というわけではない」と、その科学者は言った。
“ ___ the glow of light,” said the scientist.

子供たちは、それが当然の姿だが、身近な友人たちに、より多くの注意を向けた。
Kids paid more attention to ___ .

どんな本が子供たちの関心を引くかは、年齢次第で大きな差がある。
The ___ is great depending on their ages.
Researchers published the first global atlas of ocean light pollution.
qs.note: 第1段落の通り、世界初の海洋光害の地図を発表した。

qs.q: Artificial light at night affects only sea creatures, not land animals.
qs.note: 陸の生き物(land dwellers)にも影響する＝受粉妨害・ホタル・スズメなど。

qs.q: Tim Smyth works at a marine laboratory in California.
qs.note: Plymouth Marine Laboratory（イングランド南岸）勤務。

qs.q: Copepods normally use the sun or the winter moon as a cue.
qs.note: 通常は太陽や冬の月を手がかりにする。

qs.q: Light pollution is strongest in the top meter of the water.
qs.note: 水面付近(上から約1m)で最も強い。

qs.q: The team described its findings in the Journal of Neuroscience.
qs.note: 発表先は Elementa: Science of the Anthropocene。Journal of Neuroscience は Unit 2。

qs.q: Young kids' brains are more tuned in to their mothers' voices than to strangers'.
qs.note: 幼児期は母の声に強く反応する(思春期で逆転)。

qs.q: The shift in voice preference seems to happen between ages 13 and 14.
qs.note: 13〜14歳の間に変化が起こる。

qs.q: Stress hormones dropped when stressed-out girls heard their moms' voices on the phone.
qs.note: 2011年の研究：電話の声でストレスホルモンが低下。

qs.q: Text messages from moms had the same calming effect as phone calls.
qs.note: テキストでは同じ効果は得られなかった(The same wasn't true for texts)。

qs.q: As we mature, our survival depends more and more on maternal support.
qs.note: 成熟するにつれ母親の支援への依存は less and less(減る)。

qs.q: Daniel Abrams is a neuroscientist at Stanford University School of Medicine.
qs.note: スタンフォード大学医学部の神経科学者。

qs.q: According to the research, what kind of voices do teenagers begin to pay more attention to as they grow up?
qs.note: 思春期には見知らぬ声(unfamiliar/strangers' voices)に注意が向く。

qs.q: Why are young kids' brains very tuned in to their mothers' voices?
opts: Because they rely on maternal support for survival.
qs.ans: Because they rely on maternal support for survival.
qs.note: 幼児は生存(survival)のため母親の支援に強く依存しているから。

qs.q: What was the purpose of using nonsense words (teebudieshawlt, etc.) in the experiment?
opts: To study the voices on their own, not what was said.
qs.ans: To study the voices on their own, not what was said.
qs.note: 言葉の意味ではなく「声そのもの」を調べるため。

qs.q: "This shift" (L.26) refers to the change in the ___ of teenagers' brains to voices.
qs.note: 声に対する脳の「反応(response)」の変化。

qs.q: Approximately how long does puberty last?
qs.note: It lasts roughly a decade(約10年)。

qs.q: What does Tim Smyth study as a marine biogeochemist?
opts: How life in the oceans interacts with the environment.
How to build offshore oil rigs.
qs.ans: How life in the oceans interacts with the environment.
qs.note: 海の生命が環境とどう関わり合うかを、生物・化学・地質学で研究する。

qs.q: What were the two factors that affect how far downward light travels in water?
opts: Sediment and tiny floating plants and animals
qs.ans: Sediment and tiny floating plants and animals
qs.note: 水中の沈殿物(sediment)と微小な浮遊する動植物。
